The Buoys of October!
Managed by the Upstate Freshwater Institute (UFI) since 2019, this buoy network has been enhanced and built out to better collect data along the southern shore of Lake Ontario. Learn all about these buoys: glos.org/buoys-of-the...

Check out this fantastic video about what it takes to deploy a buoy on Lake Michigan. Video created by the super talented Freshwater Sciences Masters student Daniel Wroblewski - danielwroblewski.com/pastwork/pul... If you are coming to #IAGLR25, come see the facilities for yourself, visit June 4th!

#SeaGrant is a smart investment!🌊 #MNSG funds research using meteorological buoys that provide real-time data for National Weather Service forecasting, marine safety, fishing charters + more, adding to 11 years of #LakeSuperior data.🧪📈 Learn more about the project: z.umn.edu/mnsg-buoys
Are we laying buoys in the great lakes?

The Buoy of March!
The South Michigan Spotter is one of the stars of Winter-time Observations in the Great Lakes, providing valuable insights during what are traditionally data-sparse time periods.
Take a look at all of the data and favorite this buoy on seagull.glos.org!

The Buoys of Summer Sitting at the University of Windsor, RAEON provides infrastructure, staff, and data management that allows for cutting-edge research on the Great Lakes. Visit our website to learn more about these buoys and other observation work RAEON does: glos.org/raeon-at-the...

THOSE BUOYS! Those are BIG - too big for the Menomonee river...
I saw a yellow one - nearly 3ft. Where the F*ck did they come from!? I traced the river all the way back to Mill Pond Plaza park in Menomonee Falls using google maps. Cant place them... Lake Michigan level buoys.

Buoy oh buoy, do we have a #research update for you!🛟 MNSG-funded researcher Jay Austin has deployed 3 meteorological buoys in the western arm of #LakeSuperior. These buoys collect valuable data about the lake & share it in almost real-time! 🧪 Learn all a-buoy-t the project: z.umn.edu/mnsg_buoys

What’s #LakeSuperior up to right now? Real-time buoy data—funded by #Minnesota Sea Grant—has the scoop:
💨 Wind speed
🌡️ Water & air temps
🌊 Wave height
...and more! Perfect for fishers, paddlers, swimmers, weather nerds & Superior superfans. Dive into the science🧪👉 www.d.umn.edu/buoys/

.bsky.social GLRC has three full size buoys on Lake Superior in 2026, providing a wide array of parameters, including some novel water chemistry and quality measurements, and giving a better understanding of what happens out on the biggest of the big lakes.

For over a decade, the Great Lakes Center has operated a data buoy in Lake Erie’s eastern basin. Popular with boaters, it will soon be joined by a sibling–another buoy deployed near the city of Buffalo. Learn more➡️ PC: Brian Haas #LakeErie 🐟
I boosted that because that buoy is supposed to be out in Lake Michigan. Why it is where it is in the photo is anyone's guess, but now there's a record of it.

Educators, welcome back! 🍎 For #WaterQualityMonth, give your classroom a dose of real-time science. MNSG-funded buoys provide live data on #LakeSuperior, from wave height to water temp. It's a great lesson resource! Learn more: z.umn.edu/mnsg-buoys #EduSky #WaterSky
